newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges shade softer, cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges shade softer, cargoes steady.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges started the day a shade softer on Friday but later talked steady, with traders saying demand was picking up.

Prompt high sulphur barges changed hands between $82 and $82.50 a tonne fob ARA, compared with Thursday's late level of $83, while July barges were traded at $83 and $83.50, a touch lower than a day earlier.
But late talk was a little higher, with selling interest at $83.50/$84 and buying interest at $83, trades said.
"We heard a lot of demand in Rotterdam and a little less in Antwerp. We also had a lot of bunker enquiries," a second trader said.
Bunkers were largely steady done at $85/$86 delivered on board for 380 CST while 180 CST fetched $90.
One trader put bunker demand at some 12,000 tonnes by mid-day.
High sulphur cargoes were steady after a cargo changed hands on Thursday at $75 fob a tonne for one half and the second 50 percent at about high fob plus $3.
One Russian cracked cargo was heard on offer at two means plus $1 with a bid coming in at 50 cents lower.

A trading house was still heard to be holding a large cargo in Bilbao but traders said that with buying interest low for the lower quality material that cargo may move trans-Atlantic soon, leaving prompt avails in the Mediterranean a little on the low side.
Rumours that the cargo had been picked up by a Spanish refiner were quickly denied by the refiner, with a trader there adding: "We did not even look at that cargo, let alone buy it."
Russian high sulphur straight-run was being shown at steady prices, with only two pieces of M-100 and M-100/E4 said to be actively offered, the former at two means plus $3.50.
